processing_steps.method: high-temperature treatment (solution treatment) followed by water quench
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: This is the 'Q*' condition (water quench from 1100 °C) applied to the (111)/[112] Fe-16%Al monocrystal. Per b0015, heat treatments at 1100 °C were usually only 15 min and (except for short treatments up to 300 °C) specimens were enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsules. Quenching from 1100 °C suppresses short-range order nearly completely and traps excess vacancies.

Anneal after the 1100 °C water quench, intended to heal out excess vacancies. Reported to only slightly reduce the quenched hardness; 14 days at 300 °C may not be sufficient for complete elimination of the excess vacancies. (b0015 states that heat treatments at temperatures up to 300 °C were performed in argon of 99.99% purity.)

structures.overall_structure: Single-crystal (Bridgman-grown) Fe-16%Al monocrystal; no grain boundaries; contains rare globular AlN inclusions; after 1100 °C quench + 300 °C/14 d anneal it retains quenched-in excess vacancies (only partially healed out).

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm

defect_interactions.interaction_type: excess vacancies acting as obstacles to dislocation movement
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Excess vacancies produced by the 1100 °C quench are immobile at low temperature, are effective obstacles to dislocation movement and contribute to hardening; they are only slowly healed out by the 300 °C/14 d anneal.

interfaces.interface_notes: The sample is a monocrystal with no grain boundaries; the only second phase are rare globular AlN inclusions (up to 30 µm). Interfaces were not further characterized in this work.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: prior heat treatment: water quench from 1100 °C (Q*) + 300 °C/14 d anneal; HU defined as HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; values are averages of >40 measurements

hardness.value: > 2050 N/mm² (highest of the plotted heat-treatment conditions; above the 2050 N/mm² gridline)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: uniaxial compression; prior heat treatment: water quench from 1100 °C + 300 °C/14 d anneal; 0.2% proof-stress method with total straining of at least 5%

yield_strength.value: ≈ 450–500 MPa (plateau of the highest curve, between the 450 and 500 MPa gridlines)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Compressive stress-strain curve at RT and 10^-4 s^-1 for the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal after 1100 °C Q + 300 °C/14 d: steep elastic rise, knee at roughly 1.5–2% strain, then a nearly flat plateau with only slight hardening out to ~5.5% strain, at the highest stress level of the four heat-treatment curves (~450–500 MPa).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester (maximum load 1 N)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²] with indentation force F and depth h; reported HU values are averages of more than 40 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the effect of prior heat treatment (including 1100 °C Q + 300 °C/14 d) on the hardness of (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals
characterization_methods.key_findings: Heat treatment changes HU by only about 5–10% around 2000 N/mm²; the 1100 °C Q + 300 °C/14 d condition shows the highest hardness (>2050 N/mm²). Short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, compression rate 10^-4 s^-1; specimen dimensions 5×5×10 mm; monocrystals polished with 3 µm diamond paste; 0.2% proof stress
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the compressive stress-strain behaviour of the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal as a function of prior heat treatment
characterization_methods.key_findings: The '1100°C Q + 300°C/14d' condition gives the highest plateau stress (~450–500 MPa); the effect of heat treatment on the flow stress is only modest.

unmapped_findings: Sample composition (Table 1, monocrystal nominal 16 at.% Al): real Al content 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), impurities C 45 wt.ppm, Si 40 wt.ppm, O 60 wt.ppm.

Quenching from 1100 °C produces excess vacancies that contribute to hardening; the 300 °C anneal after quenching reduces the quenched hardness only slightly, and even 14 days at 300 °C may not be sufficient for complete elimination of the excess vacancies (slow healing-out kinetics).

The present results contrast with Davies, who reported a 25% increase of the yield stress of a quenched Fe-16.5%Al alloy by a short 1 h anneal at 300 °C (alloy preparation and impurity content not given).

Related but distinct treatment (NOT this sample's 300 °C anneal): no carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C; without any heat treatment no carbides were found in any monocrystal (b0026).
